By Anthony Fenech
Detroit Free Press

LAKELAND, Fla. – If the first thing you noticed when walking into the Detroit Tigers’ clubhouse at Joker Marchant Stadium on Wednesday was a sign displaying the team’s intentions to win the World Series, then the first thing you noticed on Thursday was Daniel Norris.
Norris, the Tigers’ left-hander, is beardless again. He shaved at 3:33 p.m. on Thursday – the beard’s born-time – heading to a barber, who took everything off in an hour’s time.
This time, Norris said, he did not find a Nerds rope inside, not even a stray M&M or two. Also beardless was righty Michael Fulmer, who said, “I tried to beat him to it.”

Fulmer was not in camp on Wednesday, attending his salary arbitration hearing in St. Petersburg, Fla. In typical, laid-back Fulmer fashion, he carpooled with Tigers officials to the hearing, which took place at the Vinoy Park Hotel.
“The only thing I can say is it happened,” Fulmer said. “I won’t be able to find out the ruling until later and then, I’ll talk about it more.”

Fulmer, 25, went 3-12 with a 4.69 ERA and 1.31 WHIP in an injury-shortened season in 2018. He filed at $3.4 million, while the Tigers filed at $2.8 million. In the near future, an arbitration panel will choose one of the figures as the winner.
The Tigers have not attended an arbitration hearing since 2001.
Asked if it went as expected, Fulmer said, “About 20 lawyers in a room and you sit there and look pretty, that’s about it.”

By Anthony Fenech
Detroit Free Press
MINNESOTA – Ian Kinsler has yet to be hot, Brad Ausmus said.
He said it in May, he said it in June and he said it most recently last week.
“Water finds its level,” he said. “And I think that Kinsler’s going to get hot.”
And on Thursday night, he did.

The Tigers’ second baseman led off a key four-game set with the Twins with a home run. He tied the game in the sixth inning with a RBI groundout. And he won the game in the eighth inning with a two-out RBI double.
The Tigers beat the Twins, 4-2, at Target Field.

With two strikes and two outs in the eighth inning – and the Tigers one strike away from squandering yet another late-inning opportunity – Kinsler drove a Mike Pelfrey offering off the top of the left-centerfield wall.
Yoenis Cespedes followed with a double to rightfield to score Kinsler.
It was enough for left-handed ace David Price who struggled early but finished strong and threw eight solid innings for his ninth win of the season.
Price allowed at least two baserunners in three of the first four innings but stranded them all and allowed two runs – none earned – on five hits. He walked three and struck out eight.

In the fifth inning, Nick Castellanos erred on a Brian Dozier groundball to open the inning. He scored on a Trevor Plouffe RBI single. Then, with two outs, Torii Hunter hit a smash off Castellanos’ glove to score Plouffe. Initially ruled an error, the official scorer changed it to a single.
Price retired all 10 batters he faced after Hunter’s single.
In the ninth inning, he gave way to Joakim Soria, who recorded his 20th save of the season. He allowed one hit.
With the win, the Tigers pulled within 1 ½ games of the second-place Twins in the American League Central. They trail the Royals by seven games.
